title: Work in the Metro film studios
summary: Howard says he played at Metro for a year, once on camera in 'Morosco's Penny Dance', never having mentioned it.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: Okay. Oh, here's a mention of the 111 Ballroom. It says the Black and Tan Band played there and was also in demand for playing society affairs. Paul also doubled with other musicians in playing extra dates. Paul played for a year at the Metro film studios, creating emotional backgrounds for the stars and music for comedy features. You didn't tell us about that. Tell us about working in the studios.
I played in the studios.
(inaudible) They've been giving me the credit. You never told me.
You was there, wasn't you?
I was there later, but nobody said that anybody had been there before me. They were giving me the credit.
Oh.
And you had and kept it quiet.
I did. I'd been there. I didn't think it was necessary, I guess.
And it said you played in a band for a film called, 'Morosco's Penny Dance.'
Oh, yeah. I've got that thing outside here. 'Morosco's Penny Dance.'
And you and your whole band were -- or you and the rest of the band -- it doesn't say it was your band, but were on camera too, or was it just your music that was on?
No, it was on camera.
On camera. That's marvelous. It doesn't say what year that is, so --
You couldn't get the years, stumbling around like I am. Ain't no way for you to get it.
But did you --
Just stumbling around.
You played for a lot of --
Excuse me please for stumbling. Huh?
Did you play for very many films?
Oh, yeah, a lot of films. Played for a lot of films.
That's wonderful.
But you'll have to forgive me because I can't remember all that stuff.
Well, it's interesting to know. Did you play in all at Metro or were there other studios you played in too?
No, just most of them I played was at Metro.
Uh-huh.
